+function atlasSelectedAuditSources() {
+  const catalogSources = sourceCatalogEntries();
+  return (state.audit.sources || []).map((selectedSource) => {
+    const identity = atlasResolveSourceIdentity(selectedSource, catalogSources);
+    const catalogSource = identity.ambiguous
+      ? {}
+      : identity.catalogSource || {};
+    return {
+      ...catalogSource,
+      ...selectedSource,
+      sourceKey: selectedSource.sourceKey || identity.sourceKey,
+      sourceFile:
+        selectedSource.sourceFile ||
+        identity.sourceFile ||
+        selectedSource.name ||
+        selectedSource.sourceKey ||
+        "",
+      alias: selectedSource.alias || identity.alias,
+      fields: catalogSource.fields?.length
+        ? catalogSource.fields
+        : selectedSource.fields || [],
+    };
+  });
 }

+function atlasNormalizedSourceIdentity(value) {
+  return String(value || "")
+    .trim()
+    .toLowerCase();
 }

+function atlasSourceIdentityCandidates(source) {
+  if (!source) return [];
+  if (typeof source === "string") {
+    const normalized = atlasNormalizedSourceIdentity(source);
+    return normalized ? [normalized] : [];
+  }
+  return [
+    source.sourceReferenceId,
+    source.sourceKey,
+    source.baseSourceKey,
+    source.id,
+    source.name,
+    source.sourceFile,
+    source.alias,
+  ]
+    .map(atlasNormalizedSourceIdentity)
+    .filter(Boolean)
+    .filter((value, index, values) => values.indexOf(value) === index);
 }

-.join-venn-source-label {
-  width: 100%;
-  overflow: hidden;
-  text-overflow: ellipsis;
-  white-space: nowrap;
-  padding: 0.32rem 0.55rem;
-  color: var(--text);

-  border-radius: 999px;
-  font-size: 0.76rem;
-  font-weight: 850;
-  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
+function atlasResolveSelectedSource(sourceLike) {
+  const selectedSources = atlasSelectedAuditSources();
+  const input =
+    typeof sourceLike === "string" ? { name: sourceLike } : sourceLike || {};
+  const stableKeys = [
+    input.sourceReferenceId,
+    input.sourceKey,
+    input.baseSourceKey,
+    input.id,
+  ]
+    .map(atlasNormalizedSourceIdentity)
+    .filter(Boolean);
+  const stableMatches = selectedSources.filter((source) => {
+    const sourceStableKeys = [
+      source.sourceReferenceId,
+      source.sourceKey,
+      source.baseSourceKey,
+      source.id,
+    ]
+      .map(atlasNormalizedSourceIdentity)
+      .filter(Boolean);
+    return stableKeys.some((key) => sourceStableKeys.includes(key));
+  });
+  if (stableMatches.length === 1) return stableMatches[0];
+  if (stableMatches.length > 1) return null;
+  const fallbackKeys = [input.name, input.sourceFile, input.alias]
+    .map(atlasNormalizedSourceIdentity)
+    .filter(Boolean);
+  const fallbackMatches = selectedSources.filter((source) => {
+    const sourceFallbackKeys = [source.name, source.sourceFile, source.alias]
+      .map(atlasNormalizedSourceIdentity)
+      .filter(Boolean);
+    return fallbackKeys.some((key) => sourceFallbackKeys.includes(key));
+  });
+  return fallbackMatches.length === 1 ? fallbackMatches[0] : null;
 }

+function atlasSourceStableKey(sourceLike) {
+  const source = atlasResolveSelectedSource(sourceLike) || sourceLike || {};
+  if (typeof source === "string") return atlasNormalizedSourceIdentity(source);
+  return String(
+    source.sourceReferenceId ||
+      source.sourceKey ||
+      source.baseSourceKey ||
+      source.id ||
+      source.sourceFile ||
+      source.name ||
+      "",
+  ).trim();
 }

+function atlasEnsureAuditSourceColors() {
+  const sources = state.audit.sources || [];
+  const palette =
+    Array.isArray(SOURCE_COLOR_PALETTE) && SOURCE_COLOR_PALETTE.length
+      ? SOURCE_COLOR_PALETTE
+      : ["#4d6fa9", "#b54b4b", "#2e7d5b", "#a66b11", "#7c5aa6"];
+  const used = new Set(sources.map((source) => source.color).filter(Boolean));
+  sources.forEach((source) => {
+    if (source.color) return;
+    source.color =
+      palette.find((color) => !used.has(color)) ||
+      palette[sources.indexOf(source) % palette.length];
+    used.add(source.color);
+  });
+  return sources;
 }

+function atlasIsCustomField(field) {
+  if (!field) return false;
+  const category = String(
+    field.dataCategory || field.category || field.type || field.fieldType || "",
+  ).toLowerCase();
+  return !!(
+    field.calculated ||
+    field.created ||
+    field.custom ||
+    category.includes("calculated") ||
+    category.includes("custom column") ||
+    category.includes("created column")
+  );
 }
 
+renderMiniPickerTrigger = function atlasSourceAwareMiniPickerTrigger(

"empty" : ""}" data-open-mini-picker="${esc(kind)}" data-param-name="${esc(name)}" data-picker-source="${esc(sourceFile)}" data-source-key="${esc(sourceKey)}" style="${color ? `--source-color:${esc(color)}` : ""}">${color ? '<span class="source-color-dot" aria-hidden="true"></span>' : ""}<span class="visual-picker-trigger-copy"><strong>${esc(visibleValue || label || "Choose...")}</strong>${detail ? `<small>${esc(detail)}</small>` : ""}</span><span aria-hidden="true">⌄</span></button>`;

+function atlasFieldMatchForSource(value, sourceLike) {
+  const normalized = String(value || "").trim();
+  const source = atlasSelectedAuditSources().find(
+    (candidate) =>
+      atlasSourceStableKey(candidate) === atlasSourceStableKey(sourceLike),
+  );
+  if (!source) return null;
+  const field = (source.fields || []).find((item) => {
+    const parts = fieldDisplayParts(item, source.sourceFile);
+    return [
+      parts.raw,
+      parts.vanity,
+      parts.display,
+      `${source.sourceFile}.${parts.raw}`,
+      `${source.alias || source.sourceFile}.${parts.raw}`,
+    ].includes(normalized);
+  });
+  return field
+    ? {
+        sourceFile: source.sourceFile,
+        sourceKey: atlasSourceStableKey(source),
+        color: atlasSelectedSourceColor(source),
+        kind: atlasIsCustomField(field) ? "custom" : "field",
+        field,
+      }
+    : null;
 }

+function atlasSourceMatchForValue(value, preferredSource = null) {
+  const normalized = String(value || "").trim();
+  if (!normalized) return null;
+  const direct = atlasResolveSelectedSource(normalized);
+  if (direct) {
+    return {
+      sourceFile: direct.sourceFile || direct.name,
+      sourceKey: atlasSourceStableKey(direct),
+      color: atlasSelectedSourceColor(direct),
+      kind: "source",
+    };
+  }
+  if (preferredSource) {
+    const preferredField = atlasFieldMatchForSource(
+      normalized,
+      preferredSource,
+    );
+    if (preferredField) return preferredField;
+  }
+  for (const source of atlasSelectedAuditSources()) {
+    const fieldMatch = atlasFieldMatchForSource(normalized, source);
+    if (fieldMatch) return fieldMatch;
+  }
+  return null;
 }
 
+renderLogicWithPills = function atlasRenderLogicWithSourceAndFieldPills(text) {
+  const parts = String(text || "").split(/("[^"]+")/g);
+  let activeSource = null;
+  return parts
+    .map((part) => {
+      if (!part.startsWith('"') || !part.endsWith('"')) return esc(part);
+      const value = part.slice(1, -1);
+      const match = atlasSourceMatchForValue(value, activeSource);
+      if (match?.kind === "source") activeSource = match;
+      const klass =
+        match?.kind === "custom"
+          ? "logic-pill custom-field-token"
+          : match?.kind === "field"
+            ? "logic-pill field-pill-token field-token"
+            : "logic-pill source-pill source-token";
+      const style = match
+        ? ` style="--pill-bg:${esc(match.color)};--pill-color:${esc(match.color)};--source-color:${esc(match.color)}"`
+        : "";
+      const dot = match
+        ? `<span class="source-color-dot" aria-hidden="true"></span>`
+        : "";
+      const displayValue =
+        match?.kind === "field" || match?.kind === "custom"
+          ? fieldDisplayParts(match.field || value, match.sourceFile).display
+          : value;
+      return `<span class="${klass}" data-source-key="${esc(match?.sourceKey || "")}"${style}>${dot}${esc(displayValue)}</span>`;
+    })
+    .join("");
+};

+function atlasAddStepAfter(stepId) {

+const atlasReferenceSyncBase = syncAutoReferenceSteps;
+syncAutoReferenceSteps = function syncAutoReferenceStepsWithDescendantCleanup(
+  ...args
+) {
+  const before = (state.audit.steps || []).map((step) => ({
+    id: step.id,
+    parentId: step.parentId || null,
+    reference:
+      !!step.autoGeneratedReference || step.step_type === "reference_source",
+  }));
+  const result = atlasReferenceSyncBase(...args);
+  const remaining = new Set((state.audit.steps || []).map((step) => step.id));
+  const removeIds = new Set(
+    before
+      .filter((step) => step.reference && !remaining.has(step.id))
+      .map((step) => step.id),
+  );
+  let changed = true;
+  while (changed) {
+    changed = false;
+    before.forEach((step) => {
+      if (
+        step.parentId &&
+        removeIds.has(step.parentId) &&
+        !removeIds.has(step.id)
+      ) {
+        removeIds.add(step.id);
+        changed = true;
+      }
+    });
+  }
+  if (removeIds.size)
+    state.audit.steps = (state.audit.steps || []).filter(
+      (step) => !removeIds.has(step.id),
+    );
+  if (state.selectedStepId && removeIds.has(state.selectedStepId))
+    state.selectedStepId = state.audit.steps[0]?.id || null;
+  return result;
+};

+function atlasOperatorOptionsForValueMode(valueMode, selectedOperator = "") {
+  const mode = valueMode || "values";
+  const operators =
+    mode === "blank"
+      ? ["is blank/null", "is not blank/null"]
+      : mode === "field"
+        ? [
+            "is equal to",
+            "is not equal to",
+            "is greater than",
+            "is greater than or equal to",
+            "is less than",
+            "is less than or equal to",
+          ]
+        : mode === "expression"
+          ? ["matches expression", "does not match expression"]
+          : [
+              "is equal to",
+              "is not equal to",
+              "contains",
+              "does not contain",
+              "starts with",
+              "ends with",
+            ];
+  return optionsHtml(
+    operators,
+    operators.includes(selectedOperator) ? selectedOperator : operators[0],
+  );
 }

+function atlasMiniPickerResultsHtml() {

+function atlasConditionConnectorValue(value, fallback = "AND") {
+  const normalized = String(value || "")

+  return normalized === "OR" ? "OR" : normalized === "AND" ? "AND" : fallback;

+function atlasWriteConditionList(step, conditions) {

+function atlasCreatedRefs(step) {

+  try {

+        refs.push({ ...c.fieldRef, location: "condition" });
+      if (c.compareFieldRef?.kind === "created")
+        refs.push({ ...c.compareFieldRef, location: "compare condition" });
+    });
+  } catch (_e) {}

+function atlasCreatedFieldIssuesForAudit() {
+  const entries = atlasPickerEntries(),
+    positions = new Map(entries.map((e, i) => [e.step.id, i])),
+    creators = new Map(
+      entries
+        .filter((e) => e.step.step_type === "create_column")
+        .map((e) => [e.step.id, e.step]),
+    );
+  return entries.flatMap((entry) =>

+          },
+        ];

+        (positions.get(ref.creatorStepId) ?? Infinity) >=
+        (positions.get(entry.step.id) ?? -1)
+      )

+            level: "error",
+            code: "created_field_forward_reference",
+            stepId: entry.step.id,

+function atlasLogicVirtualIndexAtOffset(offsets, value) {
+  let low = 0;
+  let high = Math.max(0, offsets.length - 2);
+  while (low < high) {
+    const middle = Math.floor((low + high) / 2);
+    if (offsets[middle + 1] <= value) low = middle + 1;
+    else high = middle;
+  }
+  return low;
 }

+function atlasLogicVirtualRange(entries, offsets, list) {
+  if (!entries.length) return { start: 0, end: 0 };
+  if (atlasLogicVirtualDragMode) return { start: 0, end: entries.length };
+  const top = Math.max(0, list.scrollTop - ATLAS_LOGIC_VIRTUAL_OVERSCAN_PX);
+  const bottom =
+    list.scrollTop + list.clientHeight + ATLAS_LOGIC_VIRTUAL_OVERSCAN_PX;
+  const start = atlasLogicVirtualIndexAtOffset(offsets, top);
+  const end = Math.min(
+    entries.length,
+    atlasLogicVirtualIndexAtOffset(offsets, bottom) + 1,
+  );
+  return { start, end: Math.max(start + 1, end) };
 }

+function atlasMeasureLogicVirtualCards(list, anchorId, anchorOffset) {
+  let changedAboveAnchor = 0;
+  list.querySelectorAll(".logic-rule-card[data-id]").forEach((card) => {
+    const style = getComputedStyle(card);
+    const measured = Math.ceil(
+      card.getBoundingClientRect().height +
+        (parseFloat(style.marginTop) || 0) +
+        (parseFloat(style.marginBottom) || 0),
+    );
+    const id = card.dataset.id;
+    const previous =
+      atlasLogicVirtualHeights.get(id) || ATLAS_LOGIC_VIRTUAL_ESTIMATED_HEIGHT;
+    if (measured > 0 && Math.abs(measured - previous) > 1) {
+      atlasLogicVirtualHeights.set(id, measured);
+      if (anchorId && card.offsetTop < anchorOffset)
+        changedAboveAnchor += measured - previous;
+    }
+  });
+  if (changedAboveAnchor) list.scrollTop += changedAboveAnchor;
 }

+    atlasLogicVirtualHeights.clear();

+function atlasRevealLogicStep(stepId, options = {}) {
+  const entries = atlasLogicVirtualEntries();

+  state.selectedStepId = stepId;

+        focusTarget.tabIndex = -1;

+  });
+  return true;

+function safeProjectPath(relativeFile) {
+  if (
+    typeof relativeFile !== "string" ||
+    !relativeFile.startsWith("css/") ||
+    !relativeFile.endsWith(".css")
+  ) {
+    throw new Error(`Invalid CSS source path in manifest: ${relativeFile}`);
+  }
+  const absolute = path.resolve(root, relativeFile);
+  const expectedRoot = `${path.resolve(cssRoot)}${path.sep}`;
+  if (!absolute.startsWith(expectedRoot))
+    throw new Error(`CSS source path escapes css/: ${relativeFile}`);
+  return absolute;
+}

+function stripCommentsAndWhitespace(value) {
+  return value.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, "").trim();
 }
 
+function validateCssStructure(source, label) {
+  let depth = 0;
+  let quote = null;
+  let comment = false;
+  for (let i = 0; i < source.length; i += 1) {
+    if (comment) {
+      if (source[i] === "*" && source[i + 1] === "/") {
+        comment = false;
+        i += 1;
+      }
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (quote) {
+      if (source[i] === "\\") {
+        i += 1;
+        continue;
+      }
+      if (source[i] === quote) quote = null;
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (source[i] === "/" && source[i + 1] === "*") {
+      comment = true;
+      i += 1;
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (source[i] === '"' || source[i] === "'") {
+      quote = source[i];
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (source[i] === "{") depth += 1;
+    if (source[i] === "}") {
+      depth -= 1;
+      if (depth < 0)
+        throw new Error(`${label} has an unmatched closing brace.`);
+    }
+  }
+  if (comment) throw new Error(`${label} has an unterminated comment.`);
+  if (quote) throw new Error(`${label} has an unterminated string.`);
+  if (depth !== 0) throw new Error(`${label} has unbalanced braces.`);
+}

+function splitTopLevelUnits(source, label) {
+  const units = [];
+  let start = 0;
+  let depth = 0;
+  let quote = null;
+  let comment = false;
+  for (let i = 0; i < source.length; i += 1) {
+    if (comment) {
+      if (source[i] === "*" && source[i + 1] === "/") {
+        comment = false;
+        i += 1;
+      }
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (quote) {
+      if (source[i] === "\\") {
+        i += 1;
+        continue;
+      }
+      if (source[i] === quote) quote = null;
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (source[i] === "/" && source[i + 1] === "*") {
+      comment = true;
+      i += 1;
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (source[i] === '"' || source[i] === "'") {
+      quote = source[i];
+      continue;
+    }
+    if (source[i] === "{") depth += 1;
+    else if (source[i] === "}") {
+      depth -= 1;
+      if (depth < 0)
+        throw new Error(`${label} has an unmatched closing brace.`);
+      if (depth === 0) {
+        let end = i + 1;
+        while (end < source.length && /\s/.test(source[end])) end += 1;
+        units.push({ start, end, text: source.slice(start, end) });
+        start = end;
+        i = end - 1;
+      }
+    } else if (source[i] === ";" && depth === 0) {
+      let end = i + 1;
+      while (end < source.length && /\s/.test(source[end])) end += 1;
+      units.push({ start, end, text: source.slice(start, end) });
+      start = end;
+      i = end - 1;
+    }
+  }
+  if (comment || quote || depth !== 0) validateCssStructure(source, label);
+  if (start < source.length)
+    units.push({ start, end: source.length, text: source.slice(start) });
+  return units.filter((unit) => stripCommentsAndWhitespace(unit.text) !== "");
 }
 
+function parseSourceFile(relativeFile, source) {
+  const tokens = [];
+  const occupied = [];
+  BEGIN_RE.lastIndex = 0;
+  let match;
+  while ((match = BEGIN_RE.exec(source))) {
+    const id = match[1];
+    END_RE.lastIndex = BEGIN_RE.lastIndex;
+    const endMatch = END_RE.exec(source);
+    if (!endMatch || endMatch[1] !== id)
+      throw new Error(
+        `Missing or mismatched ${id} end marker in ${relativeFile}.`,
+      );
+    const duplicateEnd = source
+      .slice(BEGIN_RE.lastIndex, endMatch.index)
+      .match(/ATLAS-SOURCE-UNIT:u\d+:END/);
+    if (duplicateEnd)
+      throw new Error(
+        `Unexpected source-unit end marker inside ${id} in ${relativeFile}.`,
+      );
+    tokens.push({
+      type: "existing",
+      id,
+      file: relativeFile,
+      start: match.index,
+      end: END_RE.lastIndex,
+      content: source.slice(BEGIN_RE.lastIndex, endMatch.index),
+    });
+    occupied.push([match.index, END_RE.lastIndex]);
+    BEGIN_RE.lastIndex = END_RE.lastIndex;
+  }

+function insertManifestUnit(units, entry, placement) {
+  if (placement.type === "end") {
+    units.push(entry);
+    return;
+  }
+  const index = units.findIndex(({ id }) => id === placement.id);
+  if (index < 0)
+    throw new Error(`Insertion anchor ${placement.id} does not exist.`);
+  units.splice(placement.type === "before" ? index : index + 1, 0, entry);

+function inferPlacement(parsed, newUnit, manifest) {
+  if (newUnit.directive) return newUnit.directive;
+  const previous = parsed.existing
+    .filter((item) => item.end <= newUnit.start)
+    .at(-1);
+  if (previous) return { type: "after", id: previous.id };
+  const next = parsed.existing.find((item) => item.start >= newUnit.end);
+  if (next) return { type: "before", id: next.id };
+  const configured = manifest.files?.[parsed.relativeFile]?.defaultInsert;
+  if (configured === "end") return { type: "end" };
+  const configuredMatch = /^(before|after):(u\d+)$/i.exec(configured || "");
+  if (configuredMatch)
+    return { type: configuredMatch[1].toLowerCase(), id: configuredMatch[2] };
+  throw new Error(
+    `Cannot place new CSS in ${parsed.relativeFile}. Add /* ATLAS-INSERT-AFTER:u#### */, /* ATLAS-INSERT-BEFORE:u#### */, or configure manifest.files["${parsed.relativeFile}"].defaultInsert.`,
+  );

+
+# PROJECT_CONTEXT.md
+
+> **Maintenance note:** Update this document whenever architecture, file responsibilities, version, priorities, or public function names change. Function inventories are generated from named function declarations and named arrow/function expressions; anonymous callbacks are intentionally omitted.
+
+## Application Overview
+
+**Application Name:** ATLAS Align  
+<!-- ATLAS-APP-VERSION:PROJECT-CONTEXT:BEGIN -->
+**Current Version:** v2.0.2
+<!-- ATLAS-APP-VERSION:PROJECT-CONTEXT:END -->
+
+### Purpose
+
+Business users document audit requirements using logic rows.
+
+### Technology
+
+- HTML
+- CSS
+- JavaScript
+- Express
+- PostgreSQL
+
+### Architecture
+
+- Frontend: `public/` conceptually, with the current source snapshot exposing browser assets at the project root and in `js/`, `css/`, and `sections/`.
+- Backend: `server.js` and `src/`.
+- Database: PostgreSQL, with migrations under `.launch/migrations/`.
+- Deployment: Docker and StudioShare Launch configuration.
+- Static browser asset contract: server.js exposes root CSS sources under /css before application routes; missing static assets must not resolve to the application HTML document.
+- Startup navigation contract: My Audits is the initial page and asynchronous initialization, issue rendering, and catalog loading do not navigate to another workflow page.
+- HTML partial contract: synchronous partial responses are checked for successful status, compatible HTML content type, and a markup-shaped response before insertion.
+- Logic Builder editor rendering contract: ordinary text input commits state and updates dependent preview or validation surfaces without recreating the selected-step editor DOM. Structural changes may request structural rendering. This preserves the active control, caret, selection, and in-progress value during typing.
+- Logic Builder field-picker eligibility contract: the selected field source controls display and selected-entry recognition, while a separate transient eligibility scope controls available entries. Multi-source IF condition fields and IF action target/value fields use all selected audit sources; intentionally source-bound controls retain single-source scope. A blank field does not imply a selected source.
+- Source-derived runtime contract: catalog lookups and source-usage inclusion are transient, versioned, explicitly invalidated performance aids. Persisted audit and catalog documents remain authoritative.
+- Audit application contract: one accepted database response applies one coherent state transition and one target-page render; stale overlapping load responses are ignored. Optional assignment profile hydration is deduplicated and audit-keyed.
+- Assignment picker contract: Audit Overview and missing-assignment Audit Issue fixes delegate to one role-aware adapter over the persistence-free shared Visual Picker. User lookup, deduplication, stale-audit validation, assignment mutation, issue invalidation, and persistence remain caller-owned.
+- User-profile persistence contract: Disney directory search is read-only. Search results remain transient; profiles become eligible for atlas_user_profiles persistence only when they appear in validated audit assignments, and the profile upsert shares the audit-save transaction.
+- Durable writeback contract: intentional new and duplicate audit actions create PostgreSQL records immediately. Audit edits retain 500 ms IndexedDB recovery and use a serialized PostgreSQL coordinator with a 2.5 second trailing delay, 20 second maximum dirty interval, revision-aware PUTs, stale-audit guards, and one follow-up write for edits made in flight. Save acknowledgement updates revision metadata and list/status surfaces without broad audit reapplication.
+- Frontend render scheduling contract: targeted render requests merge boolean surface flags monotonically until one scheduled flush. A later request cannot cancel work already requested in the same batch. Structural step requests use the shared scheduled flush rather than forcing an immediate flush; true full-state replacement may still use the broad render boundary.
+- Logic Builder rule-list virtualization contract: the complete hierarchy in application state remains authoritative while `#stepsList` mounts only a measured visible window plus overscan during normal interaction. Selection and navigation use stable step IDs, off-screen targets are revealed before focus, virtualization measurements remain transient, and drag preparation temporarily expands the mounted range without changing persisted audit data.
+- Application-version contract: `ATLAS_APP_VERSION` in `js/00-config-utils.js` is authoritative. Browser targets marked with `data-atlas-app-version` are populated from that constant, while `npm run version:sync` updates explicitly marked current-version references in maintained Markdown and `npm run version:check` validates them without writing. Package, API, schema, migration, database, and dependency versions remain independent.

+## Functional Map
+
+- **Audit Library:** Locate, create, load, persist, version, archive, restore, and administer Deleted Items with permanent-deletion event logging.
+- **Audit Overview:** Maintain audit identity, purpose, ownership, and related metadata.
+- **Source Library:** Browse database-backed sources, tables, aliases, and fields.
+- **Logic Builder:** Create hierarchical logic rows, joins, comparisons, transformations, and output actions.
+- **Display Fields:** Select final audit output fields independently from logic-derived usage, including display-only fields from included audit sources.
+- **Requirements Preview:** Render a canonical source-aware Fields inventory above analyst and developer logic in nested or complete-statement form. The same Fields rows feed HTML, clipboard HTML, and Excel requirements exports.
+- **Readiness Review:** Render the canonical Audit Issues result as a full-page review experience with independent severity filtering and the same safe Jump actions as the floating dialog.
+- **Publication and Export:** Save revisions and export requirements or workbook outputs.
+- **User Profiles:** Persist user identity and preferences.
+- **Tutorial System:** Provide page-specific guided walkthroughs.

+#### build-css.mjs
+
+**Purpose:** Builds the generated root `styles.css` file from ordered, individually managed CSS source units stored under `css/`. It validates source-unit markers, discovers and registers new top-level CSS rules, preserves cascade order through `css/manifest.json`, validates the generated CSS structure, and writes files atomically.
+
+**Inputs:**
+
+- `css/manifest.json`, which defines the ordered list of CSS unit IDs and their owning split CSS files.
+- Every `css/*.css` source file referenced by the manifest, configured in `manifest.files`, or present in the `css/` directory.
+
+**Outputs:**
+
+- Root `styles.css`, generated by concatenating CSS unit contents in manifest order.
+- Updated `css/manifest.json` when units are discovered, moved, or explicitly removed.
+- Updated split CSS files when previously unmarked top-level CSS is assigned a source-unit ID and wrapped in `ATLAS-SOURCE-UNIT` markers.
+
+**Supported command-line options:**
+
+- `--check`: Validates and previews the build without writing any files.
+- `--no-discover`: Fails if unmarked CSS is found instead of assigning it a new unit ID.
+- `--accept-deletions`: Confirms that manifest entries whose source units are missing may be removed from the manifest.
+
+**Named functions:**
+
+- readJson()
+- safeProjectPath()
+- stripCommentsAndWhitespace()
+- validateCssStructure()
+- splitTopLevelUnits()
+- parseSourceFile()
+- nextUnitNumber()
+- insertManifestUnit()
+- inferPlacement()
+- atomicWrite()
+- sourceFor()

+### Modular CSS
+
+#### CSS architecture and cascade contract
+
+The split files under `css/` are the editable CSS sources. The root `styles.css` file is generated output and should not be edited directly. Individual top-level CSS rules and at-rules are tracked as ordered source units using paired comments such as `ATLAS-SOURCE-UNIT:u0001:BEGIN` and `ATLAS-SOURCE-UNIT:u0001:END`. The unit's physical file indicates feature ownership, while its position in `css/manifest.json` controls final cascade order. Units from different files may therefore be interleaved in generated `styles.css`.
+
+Because later emitted rules can override earlier rules, moving a rule between files does not by itself determine precedence. Preserve or deliberately update its manifest position when changing ownership. New unmarked top-level rules are discovered by the build script and must have an unambiguous insertion location. Place them next to an existing marked unit, add an `ATLAS-INSERT-AFTER:u####` or `ATLAS-INSERT-BEFORE:u####` directive, use `ATLAS-INSERT:END`, or configure a default insertion location in the manifest.
+
+#### css/global.css
+
+**Purpose:** Owns application-wide design tokens and shared presentation rules. This includes light and dark theme variables, resets, shell and navigation layout, topbar and profile display, shared typography, cards, buttons, forms, tables, statuses, badges, generic modal and picker primitives, tutorial overlays, shared responsive rules, cross-page utilities, and reusable source/field token styling. Feature files may depend on the custom properties and base components defined here.
+
+**Use for:** A selector or visual primitive used across multiple pages, the application shell, shared controls, global accessibility behavior, or theme-level behavior.
+
+#### css/audit-overview.css
+
+**Purpose:** Owns Audit Overview assignment UI styling, including assignment columns, selected-user chips, avatars, and role-specific shared Visual Picker triggers.
+
+**Use for:** Selectors specific to audit metadata, ownership, contributor, reviewer, or assignment experiences on the Audit Overview page.
+
+#### css/group-landing.css
+
+**Purpose:** Reserved feature stylesheet for the group landing or dashboard page. It is currently empty in the supplied CSS snapshot, so the page inherits its presentation from shared rules in `css/global.css`.
+
+**Use for:** New selectors that apply only to the group landing or dashboard and should not affect other pages.
+
+#### css/logic-builder.css
+
+**Purpose:** Owns the Logic Builder workspace and its specialized interactions. It covers the rules list, variable-height rule cards, hierarchy and collapse controls, selected-step editor, IF/THEN tabs, condition and action builders, logic text wrapping, source and field pickers used by rules, join and union pickers with Venn visuals, new-rule and rule-action menus, logic issue remediation UI, calculated-field math controls, created-field indicators, linked inverse steps, page-specific scrolling, responsive behavior, and overflow containment.
+
+**Use for:** Selectors scoped to `#page-steps`, logic rules, step editing, validation/remediation surfaces launched from the builder, or builder-only picker behavior.
+
+#### css/my-audits.css
+
+**Purpose:** Owns the My Audits and Audit Library experience. It covers the audit contact/list presentation, search and filter controls, metrics, create/import actions, database loading state and spinner, table presentation, viewport-aware scrolling, responsive headers, role badges, and focus treatment for audit-library actions.
+
+**Use for:** Selectors specific to `#page-my-audits`, the visible Audit Library, audit search/filter behavior, audit tables, or audit-loading presentation.
+
+#### css/publication-preview.css
+
+**Purpose:** Owns Publication Preview and save/export presentation. The supplied snapshot currently contains the package-heading divider used to separate publication or export package sections.
+
+**Use for:** Selectors specific to the publication, packaging, save, or export preview page.
+
+#### css/readiness-review.css
+
+**Purpose:** Reserved feature stylesheet for the Readiness Review page. It is currently empty in the supplied CSS snapshot, so the page uses shared rules from `css/global.css`.
+
+**Use for:** New selectors specific to readiness checks, validation summaries, or review-only layouts that are not reused by the Logic Builder.
+
+#### css/display-fields.css
+
+**Purpose:** Owns Display Fields table, switch, empty-state, responsive, theme, and reduced-motion presentation. Shared picker presentation is owned by `css/visual-picker.css`.
+
+#### css/requirements-preview.css
+
+**Purpose:** Reserved feature stylesheet for the Requirements Preview page. It is currently empty in the supplied CSS snapshot, so preview tables and shared presentation are inherited from `css/global.css` and other existing shared units.
+
+**Use for:** New selectors specific to analyst/developer requirements preview layouts, statement-mode controls, or preview-only tables.
+
+#### css/sources.css
+
+**Purpose:** Owns the Sources and Fields experience. It covers Source Library dialogs and embedded lists, contact-style source browsing, selected-source cards and metadata, source color controls, source and field tables, source replacement workflows, CSV import status, field-detail panes, viewport-aware scrolling, alphabet navigation, inclusion badges, source actions, source-name wrapping, and responsive source layouts. Some legacy alignment rules that touch Logic Builder-related elements remain here because unit ownership reflects the current split history.
+
+**Use for:** Selectors specific to `#page-fields`, Source Library browsing, selected sources, field tables, source replacement, or source import behavior.
+
+#### css/manifest.json
+
+**Purpose:** Defines the authoritative CSS build order. Each entry maps a stable source-unit ID to the split CSS file containing that unit. The manifest also records its schema version, the next available unit number, the generated output filename through `source`, and optional per-file insertion defaults.
+
+**Important behavior:** The manifest order, not alphabetical file order, determines the rule order in generated `styles.css`. Do not manually renumber existing unit IDs. Let `build-css.mjs` assign IDs to newly discovered rules.
+
+#### styles.css
+
+**Purpose:** Generated browser stylesheet assembled from the ordered units in `css/manifest.json`. It is the deployable compatibility artifact consumed by the application and must be regenerated after changes to split CSS files.
+
+**Editing rule:** Do not make source changes directly in `styles.css`; those changes can be overwritten by the next build. Edit the appropriate `css/*.css` file and rebuild instead.
+
+#### How to build the CSS
+
+**Prerequisites:**
+
+- Run the command from the project root, where `build-css.mjs`, `styles.css`, and the `css/` directory are siblings.
+- Use a Node.js environment that supports ECMAScript modules and the `node:` built-in import specifiers used by the script.
+
+**Recommended workflow:**
+
+1. Edit the appropriate split stylesheet under `css/`.
+2. Preview validation and discovery without writing files:
+
+```bash
+node build-css.mjs --check
+```
+
+3. Review any reported missing units, newly discovered units, insertion placements, or structural errors.
+4. Build and write the generated output:
+
+```bash
+node build-css.mjs
+```
+
+5. Review changes to the edited split CSS file, `css/manifest.json`, and root `styles.css` before committing them together.
+6. Run a strict verification that no unmarked CSS remains:
+
+```bash
+node build-css.mjs --check --no-discover
+```
+
+**Deletion workflow:** If a marked CSS unit was intentionally removed from its split source file, first preview the confirmed deletion without writing:
+
+```bash
+node build-css.mjs --check --accept-deletions
+```
+
+Then apply the deletion to the manifest and generated stylesheet:
+
+```bash
+node build-css.mjs --accept-deletions
+```
+
+Do not use `--accept-deletions` merely to bypass an unexpected missing-unit error. Restore the missing marked unit or investigate the manifest mismatch unless deletion was intentional.
+
+**Expected success output:** A normal build reports that `styles.css` was built from the ordered source units. Check mode reports that the CSS check passed and states how many units would be emitted. If new unmarked rules were found, the script reports the assigned IDs and their placements.
+
+**Build safety behavior:** The script rejects unknown options, unsafe paths, missing source files, invalid or duplicate unit IDs, mismatched or orphaned markers, ambiguous insertion locations, unbalanced CSS syntax, duplicate output emission, and generated output that still contains source-management markers. Writes use temporary files followed by rename operations.

+## Dependency and Load-Order Notes
+
+- Browser modules rely on ordered script loading and a shared global runtime. Earlier numbered files establish utilities and state used by later modules.
+- `00-html-partials-loader.js` loads page partials before modules cache DOM references and bootstrap the application.
+- Database-backed source, audit, revision, and profile behavior spans `server.js`, `src/`, and `.launch/migrations/`.
+- CSS is edited in feature-oriented files under `css/`; `css/manifest.json` preserves unit-level cascade order across those files, and `node build-css.mjs` generates root `styles.css`.
+

+

+- `isOpen()`
+
+### `catalogs/audit-issue-rules.json`
+
+**Purpose:** Defines declarative Audit Issue rule metadata, including stable IDs, enabled state, severity, category, priority, user-facing text, named evaluator/action references, target type, configuration, and documentation. The catalog contains no executable code. Enabled entries are evaluated by named ATLAS adapter evaluators and actions; the catalog remains declarative and contains no executable code.
+
+### `js/22-audit-issue-engine.js`
+
+**Purpose:** Provides the portable, persistence-free Audit Issue engine. The classic-script IIFE exposes `AuditIssueEngine` without reading ATLAS state or DOM. Caller-provided named registries supply evaluators and optional actions.
+
+**Public API:**
+
+- `AuditIssueEngine.create(options)` creates an independent engine instance.
+- `AuditIssueEngine.validateRules(rules, registries)` validates and normalizes declarative rules.
+- `AuditIssueEngine.severities` exposes the supported severity names.
+
+**Engine instance API:**
+
+- `evaluate(context, rules)` validates rules, evaluates enabled rules, isolates evaluator failures, normalizes/deduplicates/sorts issues, and returns immutable issues, aggregate status, and counts.
+- `validateRules(rules)` validates rules against that instance's named registries.
+- `aggregate(issues)` returns immutable `ok`, `warning`, or `critical` status and counts.
+- `severities` exposes supported severity names.
+
+**Architecture contract:** Issue engine inputs and outputs are transient and caller-owned. The engine must remain independent from `state.audit`, ATLAS globals and selectors, navigation, persistence, rendering, exports, APIs, databases, and authorization. Catalog strings must never be evaluated as code.
+
+### `test/audit-issue-engine.test.js`
+
+**Purpose:** Provides deterministic Node tests for catalog parsing, independent instances, rule validation, normalization, immutability, deduplication, ordering, severity aggregation, disabled rules, evaluator isolation, and invalid-catalog rejection.
+
+### `js/23-atlas-audit-issues.js`
+
+**Purpose:** Provides the ATLAS-specific adapter for the portable Audit Issue engine. It normalizes the active audit without mutation, loads `catalogs/audit-issue-rules.json`, registers named ATLAS evaluators and future navigation actions, maintains a transient signature-and-generation cache, and exposes the canonical issue result used by compatibility validation callers.
+
+**Public API:**
+
+- `ATLASAuditIssues.buildContext(audit)` returns normalized, caller-independent issue context.
+- `ATLASAuditIssues.current()` returns the canonical immutable issue result.
+- `ATLASAuditIssues.invalidate()` invalidates the transient cache.
+- `ATLASAuditIssues.legacyIssues()` maps canonical issues to the legacy `level` and `message` shape.
+- `ATLASAuditIssues.loadCatalog()` loads and validates the declarative catalog for evaluation.
+- `ATLASAuditIssues.catalogReady` identifies the active catalog-load promise.
+- `atlasLogicIssues()` is a compatibility function returning canonical normalized issues.
+- `atlasMarkLogicIssuesDirty()` delegates to canonical cache invalidation.
+
+**Validation ownership:** `js/08-step-templates-validation.js` retains legacy template behavior and Readiness rendering, but `validateAudit()` now delegates to `ATLASAuditIssues.legacyIssues()`. Math, string-transform, created-field, and Logic Builder issue wrapper chains in later visual scripts no longer form separate active issue collections; their proven helper validators remain available to the ATLAS evaluator registry.
+
+**Rule behavior:** The catalog enables verified audit setup, assignment, source/reference, hierarchy, condition, action, join, calculation, string-transform, created-field, workbook-warning, and Display Fields checks. The field-relationship rule is enabled and treats enabled, complete INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, and FULL OUTER JOIN steps as undirected source relationships. Direct and indirect JOIN paths are valid; UNION, disabled, incomplete, unsupported, and ambiguously resolved JOIN steps do not establish connectivity. Complete field comparisons between distinct, resolved, selected sources without a JOIN path produce a critical Jump-only issue.
+
+### Floating Audit Issues presentation
+
+- `sections/audit-issues.html` and `css/audit-issues.css` own the single floating audit-status control and accessible shared issue dialog.
+- `js/23-atlas-audit-issues.js` renders the floating dialog and Readiness & Review from the same transient canonical result, coalesces refreshes, and owns filter/focus lifecycle without navigation or mutation.
+- `sections/readiness-review.html` and `css/readiness-review.css` own the Readiness-only canonical summary, category status, and layout.
+- The documented application version remains v2.0; the request template's managed current-version references are synchronized from `ATLAS_APP_VERSION`.
+
+### Audit Issue navigation and safe remediation policy
+
+- `js/23-atlas-audit-issues.js` owns named Jump actions for Audit Overview metadata/assignments, Sources, Logic Builder, Display Fields, and Readiness & Review.
+- Logic targets use stable step IDs with `atlasRevealLogicStep()` before editor focus so virtualized steps can be revealed safely.
+- Jump actions verify the active audit key and canonical stable issue key immediately before navigation. A stale issue does not mutate state and triggers canonical refresh.
+- Phase 4 enables no inline fixes because the reviewed missing values require user-selected text/options or ambiguous business decisions. Assignment, source/field, relationship, hierarchy, and removed-reference issues remain navigation-only.
+- `validateAudit()`, `renderValidationPanel()`, and `atlasLogicIssues()` remain documented compatibility surfaces backed by the canonical issue result.
+- Critical issues remain advisory; publication behavior is unchanged.
+
+- Safe remediation remains action-registry controlled. No rule receives a Fix action unless current source proves a deterministic or bounded user-confirmed mutation through an existing owning workflow; otherwise the issue remains Jump only and no disabled generic Fix is shown.
+
+
+#### In-place Audit Issue remediation
+- `js/23-atlas-audit-issues.js` registers bounded named Fix actions for missing Audit Description, assignment roles, source selection, and targeted JOIN issues. Both issue surfaces render Fix only for registered actions; unsupported or ambiguous issues remain Jump-only.
+- `js/16-page-shell.js` exposes `ATLASAssignmentEditor`; `js/15f-join-picker.js` exposes `ATLASJoinPicker`.
+
